title: Gemini gateway adapter: thoughtSignature is a sibling of functionCall on the Part, never nested inside it
answers: Gemini multi-turn tool calling through the AI Gateway fails or is rejected because thoughtSignature is missing or misplaced
Why is the thought signature dropped from tool call responses returned by the gateway chat endpoint for Gemini models?
Where does the gateway convert tool calls and thought signatures to and from Gemini's contents/parts format?
How do I pass a thought_signature from an OpenAI-style tool call back to a Gemini or Vertex AI model?
body:
Path: Gemini AI Gateway chat requests and responses (tool/function calling, multi-turn history) pass through mlflow/gateway/providers/gemini.py:GeminiAdapter. Outbound, GeminiAdapter.chat_to_model turns OpenAI-style assistant tool_calls into Gemini model `parts`. Inbound, GeminiAdapter._convert_function_call_to_openai_choice turns Gemini `functionCall` parts into OpenAI tool_calls.
Rule: Gemini places `thoughtSignature` on the Part, next to `functionCall`, not inside it. chat_to_model builds `part = {"functionCall": fc}` and sets `part["thoughtSignature"]` from the tool call id map, then appends `part`. On read, _convert_function_call_to_openai_choice checks `part` for thoughtSignature/thought_signature first and falls back to the nested `function_call` keys only for older responses.
Symptom: On the second turn of a tool-calling conversation, Gemini rejected the request because the signature was nested inside functionCall. On responses, the signature was silently missing from tool_calls, so clients could not send it back.
Constraints: Applies to the Gemini adapter's functionCall handling. Do not add thoughtSignature to the functionCall dict on write. Tests in tests/gateway/providers/test_gemini.py (test_gemini_chat_function_calling_thought_signature and the parametrized test_gemini_function_call_thought_signature_response) cover both placements on read.
applies: Gateway Gemini provider: any change to tool-call request building or response parsing, including thought signature round-trips in multi-turn conversations.
says: Multi-turn chat conversations using Gemini tools fail after the first function call.
Gemini rejects follow-up requests during multi-turn agent chats that involve tool calling.
Model thought signatures are dropped from gateway chat responses when calling tools.
Preserve thought signatures in tool responses so conversational agents can resume multi-turn tasks.
Second turn tool calls to Gemini return rejection errors from the gateway.
search: In `mlflow.gateway.providers.gemini.GeminiAdapter`, `thoughtSignature` must be placed alongside `functionCall` as a sibling property on the Gemini `part`, never nested inside the `functionCall` dictionary. `GeminiAdapter.chat_to_model` attaches `thoughtSignature` directly to the `part` dictionary from the tool call ID map when converting OpenAI assistant `tool_calls`. `GeminiAdapter._convert_function_call_to_openai_choice` reads `thoughtSignature` or `thought_signature` from `part` first, falling back to nested `function_call` keys only for older responses. This applies to Gemini AI Gateway chat requests and responses handling tool and function calling across multi-turn history, preventing rejected requests on second turns or missing signatures on responses.
